user_questions.question: The requirement does not say what outcome you want, and the org supports several: Refund__c (Status__c Pending/Approved/Processing/Completed/Failed/Cancelled, linked to Case via Case__c) has no automation, and every writer inserts refunds as Approved. Which should the spec deliver? (a) Alert when refunds stay too long in a status (for example Processing) - recommended, since nothing tracks refund delays today; (b) automate the refund status lifecycle; (c) reporting/visibility on refund complaints (Case Type 'Refund / Compensation'). If (a), which status, how long, and who is alerted?
user_questions.simulated_answer: Refunds sit in Processing too long; alert the case owner when a refund is Processing > 5 days.

skill_friction: The pre-D1 vagueness rule only fires when no object, process, or outcome can be identified. 'Do something about refunds' names a process but no outcome, so D1 and D2 ran before the obviously blocking scope question; the rule could say 'no outcome' alone is enough to ask, or explicitly allow asking right after D1.
The I call took 77 s, over the stated ~60 s timeout, yet returned complete; the timeout guidance is approximate and the runner schema has no way to mark 'slow but not timed out'.

AskCoworker R/T made platform-behavior claims (scheduled paths not cancelled when record stops matching; inserts never trigger 'updated to meet condition' flows; DE scheduled-path capacity blocking) that contradict documented behavior; Rule 3 covers this but no query can test it, so the corrections rest on my own platform knowledge tagged as assumption. Whether pending scheduled paths run after record delete remained unverified.
AskCoworker D2 said IssueRefundReceiptAction is the only Refund__c writer; MetadataComponentDependency found two more flows. The 'missed components' check was essential here.
